subtitle: Lesson 3 · Programming Fundamentals Through JavaScript

code:
let count = 1;        // can be reassigned later
const owner = "Ana";  // cannot be reassigned after this line
var legacy = true;    // old syntax -- avoid in new code

// Default to const. Use let only when you'll reassign it.
caption: const is the right default — it makes a script easier to reason about.

code:
let name = "Ana";            // string
let age = 29;                // number
let isActive = true;         // boolean
let nothingYet;               // undefined
let empty = null;             // null
let big = 9007199254740993n;  // bigint
caption: bigint exists because wei balances routinely exceed safe number range.

code:
typeof "Ana";      // "string"
typeof 29;         // "number"
typeof true;       // "boolean"
typeof undefined;  // "undefined"
typeof null;       // "object" -- a famous 1995 JS bug
typeof 10n;        // "bigint"
caption: typeof null returning "object" is a known quirk, not your mistake.
